title: [Object Browser] Create Additional Topstitch Style
content: **Objective** Create a new Topstitch style. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **+Add** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **+Add** → A new item named Topstitch_1 is now being added with the same property of Default_Topstitch. **※ Note:** * Additional items are added with names of Topstitch_1,2,3…. * If there are multiple Topstitch styles in the Topstitch tab when creating a Topstitch on a Pattern, click on the desired Topstitch style and create. * To create an additional Topstitch style with existing *.sst file, navigate to the Library ▶ Hardware and Trims ▶ **Topstitch** and drag and drop the desired Topstitch style to the Topstitch tab. Or, find the Topstitch file in the File Brower window and drag and drop.
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for creating and managing new Topstitch styles in the Object Browser's Topstitch tab.

title: [Style Property] Topstitch Thread Thickness
content: ### **Objective** Adjust the **Thread Thickness** in the desired measurement unit: inch, millimeter (mm), or centimeter (cm). Topstitch thickness can also be adjusted in industry standard units: Tex, Ticket (Tkt), Metric (Nm), or Denier (Den) (ver4.0.0). **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Thread Thickness** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ▶ Topstitch Property Editor ▶ **Thread Thickness** → Adjust the **Thread Thickness** with the desired unit of measurement.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to adjusting thread thickness in various measurement units for topstitching in the Topstitch Property Editor.

title: [Style Property] Save Created Image as Topstitch File
content: ### **Objective** Save customized Topstitch images in a *.sst format file. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **Default Topstitch** ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ **Default Topstitch** → Properties of the selected Topstitch appear in the Property Editor. 2. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Type and select **Texture** from the drop-down menu. 3. Under the **Material** section, select the same structured Topstitch to the one customized. 4. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture and then click on the Topstitch image icon or the **Search** button. → The Open file window appears. 5. Find the path to the customized images and select the one only with the name of Topstitch (ex. "zigzag.png") and click **Open**. → The program automatically saves all five images in *.sst file according to the defined naming rule. → The image is loaded in actual size which is approximately 2cm and it may look bigger than other preset Topstitches. 6. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Preset and enter desired value to the **Stitch Width** menu (ex. 5mm) to adjust its size. 7. On the right top of the Property Editor, there is a **Save** button. Select to save. → The Save file window appears. 8. Enter the desired name and location and save. → The Topstitch is now being saved in *.sst file format. **※ Note:** * Topstitches are classified into two different types depending on the presence and absence of the Stitch Width property. For example, when adding a zigzag-style top stitches, select Overlock or Zigzag as its width needs to be adjustable. **Without Width Property** | Default (Single Needle) ---|--- Default Offset 0 Pick Stitch **With Width Property** | Overlock Zigzag Buttonhole Bar Tack * Make sure all of the Topstitch image files are located in the same path as it will not be saved in the SST file properly. * The image is bigger than the actual size to prevent distortion in resolution when enlarging the image. * Drag and drop the saved SST file directly onto the Topstitch Item List or open it by pressing the **Open** button in the Property Editor. Adjust the property details such as the Length, Offset, Thread Thickness or Color likewise any other Topstitch styles.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to saving customized Topstitch images in the *.sst format, ensuring seamless integration and adjustment within your design projects.

title: [Style Property] Create Topstitch Image File
content: ### **Objective** Customize Topstitch images. ### **Operation ** 1. Click on the link below to download the sample Topstitch images in Photoshop file format. [Topstitch Sample Image Download](https://s3.amazonaws.com/CLOdata/Manual_Linked_File_\(DoNotDelete\)/Topstitch_Zigzag.zip) 2. Create five images of Topstitches in each different thread thickness in Adobe Photoshop. 3. Save the images followed by the rules below. →Save the images in *PNG file format. →Name the images as below: **Required File Name** | **Thread Thickness Range of Topstitch Property in Program** ---|--- ※ When modifying the thread thickness value as the right section, images will be opened as the left section. **Zigzag_vertythin.png** | 0.2 - 0.4 mm **Zigzag_thin.png** | 0.5 - 0.6 mm **Zigzag.png** | 0.7 - 1.0 mm **Zigzag_thick.png** | 1.0 - 1.5 mm **Zigzag_verythick.png** | > 1.5 mm →Save all five images in the same location. **※ Note:** * To create top-stitch images, it is needed to have editable software (ex. Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Illustrator). * To create one top-stitch, five images of each different thread thickness are required. (Five images are included in the provided Download File.) * If not creating all five images in each different thread thickness, the thread thickness is unable to be modified in spite of modifying the value in Thread Thickness in the Property Editor. * To express transparent background, the *PNG file should contains an alpha channel. [(Creating an alpha channel)](https://helpx.adobe.com/photoshop/using/saving-selections-alpha-channel-masks.html) Simply save the file after adjustments as the provided Download File already includes an alpha channel. * When saving a newly loaded Topstitch style into a file, the program automatically loads all five images and save, all of the images should be in the same path or location in order to work properly.
content_description: Create and customize Topstitch images in Adobe Photoshop by following the guidelines for downloading, modifying thread thickness, and saving in the correct format.

title: [Object Browser] Puckering List Window
content: It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in puckering list window. Without any extra setting, Default_Puckering is applied as default. Once Default_Puckering style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.
content_description: This webpage provides guidance on creating, copying, and applying styles in the puckering list window, highlighting the default behavior of the Default_Puckering style and its modifications.

title: [Object Browser] Create Additional Puckering Style
content: ### **Objective** Create a new Puckering style. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab ▶ **Add** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Puckering Tab ▶ **Add**** **→ A new Puckering style with the same properties as Default_Puckering is now being added. **※Note:** To create an additional Puckering style with existing *.ptp file, navigate to the folder contains the desired *.ptp file. Then, drag and drop the desired Puckering style to the Puckering tab. Or, find the Puckering file in the File Browser window and drag and drop.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating a new Puckering style in the Object Browser, ensuring users can easily replicate and customize existing styles.

title: [Style Property] Number of Topstitch Line Setting
content: ### **Objective** Set how many lines of Topstitches there are for a single style. ** Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Number of Lines** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Property Editor ▶ **Number of Lines** 2. Enter the number of lines as desired. → The **Number of Lines** is now being adjusted and applied. **※ Note :** **Distance of Number of Lines** It is possible to adjust the distance between the lines. The unit of the length can be set in inch, millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm). When alteration is made in inch(in), it automatically appears in millimeter(mm) or centimeter(cm) and vice versa.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on setting and adjusting the number of Topstitch lines for a specific style, including distance measurements in various units.

title: Copy
content: **List of Contents** Copy Copy a Pattern Copy an Internal Shape **Copy** \- Copy Patterns and Internal Shapes. ** Copy a Pattern** \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Pattern to be duplicated and select **Copy.** \- The selected Pattern will be duplicated. **Copy an Internal Shape** \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated and select **Copy.** \- The selected Internal Shape will be duplicated. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for copying patterns and internal shapes using the 2D toolbar tools in Clo3D.

title: Avatar Rendering Style
content: **List of Contents** Avatar Rendering Style Textured Surface Mesh Monochrome Surface **Avatar Rendering Style** \- Display Avatars in various Rendering Styles. \- Navigate to the 3D window and hover over the last icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu. ** Textured Surface** \- When an Avatar is loaded, the Textured Surface is applied to the Avatar by default, showing the skin texture of the Avatar. **Mesh** \- Click the Mesh option to see Avatars’ Mesh structure. **Monochrome Surface** \- Click the Monochrome Surface option to see Avatars in black and white. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore different avatar rendering styles, including textured surfaces, mesh structures, and monochrome views, to enhance your 3D experience.

title: Import - OBJ
content: **List of Contents** Import OBJ Import (Add) OBJ **Import OBJ** \- OBJs can be used as Avatars or other background props compose the 3D environment. \- The 3D Garments created in CLO can be exported as an OBJ to use in other 3D software. \- When a 3D Garment is exported as an OBJ, the file will contain MTL file which saves the texture information. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import ▶ **OBJ. ** \- Locate the OBJ file and select **Open.** \- The Import OBJ window will appear. \- **Load Type** : Select either to open or add the OBJ file. \- **Object Type** : select the type of the OBJ file \- **Scale** : select the unit of the OBJ When the**Auto Scale** option is selected, CLO will detect the unit of the OBJ automatically. \- Axis Conversion: Change the axis of the OBJ. \- Translation: designate the position of the OBJ. \- Select OK to open the OBJ based on the settings. ** Import (Add) OBJ** \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ **OBJ. ** \- Locate the OBJ file and select **Open.** \- The selected OBJ file will be added to the workspace. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on importing OBJ files into CLO, detailing the steps and options for effectively integrating 3D avatars and garments into your projects.

title: New
content: **List of Contents** New Create a New File **New ** \- Delete the Garment in the current workspace and create a new Garment. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ File ▶ **New.** ** Create a New File** \- The **New** option is activated only when a file is already open. \- Navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ File ▶ **New.** \- The dialogue asking to save the current file will pop up. \- Select the desired option and the current file will either be saved or deleted based on the selection and a new file will open. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to create a new garment file while managing your current workspace effectively.

title: Divide Internal Lines
content: **List of Contents** Divide Internal Point Divide Internal Line **Objective** Cut and separate Internal Lines or points from an Internal Shape or continuous Internal Line. ** Location** **Divide Internal Point** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Point) ▶ **Divide Internal Point** ** Divide Internal Line** Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Line) ▶ **Divide Internal Line** ** Operation** **Divide Internal Point** 1. Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001095927/2.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Point) ▶**Internal Point** → The Internal Line is divided at the selected point. → The divided point is now indicated as a point with no fill. **Divide Internal Line** 1. Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001095927/2.png)**Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Line) ▶ **Divide Internal Line** → The Internal Line is divided from its original Internal Shape. → Both ends of the Internal Line are indicated with points with no fill. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for dividing internal points and lines within a shape using the Edit Pattern tool in Clo3D.

title: Zoom Extents All
content: **List of Contents** Zoom Extents All Result of Zoom Extents All **Zoom Extents All** \- See all Patterns in the 3D window without changing the view in the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D window and select **Zoom Extents All.** ** Result of Zoom Extents All** \- Right-click on the 3D window and select **Zoom Extents All.** \- The 3D window will scale automatically to show all Patterns. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides guidance on using the "Zoom Extents All" feature to view all patterns in a 3D window without altering the current view.

title: Mirror Paste
content: **List of Contents** Mirror Paste Mirror Paste with Specific Values **Mirror Paste** \- Mirror Paste copied Patterns and Internal Shapes. * **Mirror Paste a Pattern **\- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Pattern to be duplicated and select **Copy.** \- The selected Pattern will be duplicated. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Mirror Paste** from the pop-up menu. \- The duplicated Pattern will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click on the 2D window to Mirror Paste the Pattern. \- The identical Pattern will be created in the 2D window. * **Mirror Paste an Internal Shape ** \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated and select **Copy.** \- The selected Internal Shape will be duplicated. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Mirror Paste** from the pop-up menu. \- The duplicated Internal Shape will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Click within the Pattern to Mirror Paste the Internal Shape. \- The identical Internal Shape will be created in the 2D window. **Mirror Paste with Specific Values** * **Mirror Paste a Pattern** \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. \- Right-click on the Pattern to be duplicated and select **Copy.** \- The selected Pattern will be duplicated. \- Right click on the 2D window and select **Mirror Paste** from the pop-up menu. \- The duplicated Pattern will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Right-click on the 2D window to access the Paste pop-up window. \- Enter the desired values to **Internal** and **Number of Shapes**. Then, click OK. 。 \- The Pattern will be mirror pasted based on the settings. * **Mirror Paste an Internal Shape ** \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) Edit Pattern tool. \- Right-click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated and select **Copy**. \- The selected Internal Shape will be duplicated. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Mirror Paste** from the pop-up menu. \- The duplicated Internal Shape will follow along the mouse cursor. \- Right-click on the 2D window to access the Paste pop-up window. \- Enter the desired values to Interval, Number of Shapes, and Position. Then, click OK. \- The Internal Shape will be mirror pasted based on the settings. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to use the Mirror Paste feature in the 2D toolbar for duplicating patterns and internal shapes in CLO 3D, including instructions for specific value adjustments.

title: Show All Piping
content: **Show All Piping** \- Show all Pipings in the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D window and select **Show All Piping** from the pop-up menu. \- All Pipings in the 3D window will appear.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to guide users on how to display all piping in the 3D window by using the right-click context menu.

title: Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected)
content: **Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected)** \- Re-arrange 3D Patterns according to the Pattern arrangement in the 2D window. \- Right-click on the Pattern to be re-arranged and select **Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected)** from the pop-up menu. \- Selected Patterns will be re-arranged in the 3D window reflecting the Pattern arrangement in the 2D window.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with instructions for re-arranging selected 3D patterns to match their arrangement in the 2D window using the "Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected)" feature.

title: Flip Normal
content: **Flip Normal** \- Easily flip the Pattern inside-out. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select **Flip Normal.** \- The selected Pattern will flip inside-out, face side will flip to the backside and vice-versa. \- When Fold Angles are assigned to the flipped Pattern, Fold Angles will be reversed.
content_description: The "Flip Normal" page provides a simple guide for users to easily flip the pattern of their garment inside-out within the 3D design interface.

title: Pin – Delete All Pins
content: **Pin - Delete All Pins** \- Delete all pins on the 3D Garment. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select****/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and Select pin ▶ **Delete All Pins.** \- All pins created on the 3D Garment will be deleted.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to delete all pins from a 3D garment in the design software.

title: Lock All Internal Lines
content: **Lock All Internal Lines** \- Lock all Internal Lines to inhibit selecting and editing in the 2D window. \- Right-click on the 2D window and select **Lock All Internal Lines** from the pop-up menu. All Internal Lines will turn grey and be deactivated. \- Only activated Patterns can be selected and edited.
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for locking all Internal Lines in the 2D window to prevent selection and editing, ensuring only activated Patterns remain editable.

title: Superimpose (Under)
content: **Superimpose (Under)** \- When a Pattern is sewn to another Pattern, place one below the other’s surface based on the Sewing Lines. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select****/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select **Superimpose (Under).** \- The selected Pattern will be arranged under the sewn pair along its surface. \- The Superimpose (Under) function can be used only when two Patterns are sewn to each other.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to use the Superimpose (Under) function to arrange one Pattern beneath another in a 3D garment design.

title: Superimpose (Side)
content: **Superimpose (Side)** \- When a Pattern is sewn to another Pattern, place one next to the other’s side based on the Sewing Lines. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/****Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select Superimpose (Side). \- The selected Pattern will be arranged next to the sewn pair along its side. \- The Superimpose (Side) function can be used only when two Patterns are sewn to each other.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on using the Superimpose (Side) feature to align sewn patterns in a 3D garment design.

title: Superimpose (Over)
content: **Superimpose (Over)** \- When a Pattern is sewn to another Pattern, place one above the other’s surface based on the Sewing Lines. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select **Superimpose (Over).** \- The selected Pattern will be arranged above the sewn pair along its surface. \- The Superimpose (Over) function can be used only when two Patterns are sewn to each other.
content_description: Learn how to effectively use the Superimpose (Over) function in garment design to layer patterns accurately based on sewing lines.

title: Flip Vertically (2D)
content: **Flip Vertically (2D)** \- Flip a Pattern vertically in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the Pattern to be flipped and select **Flip Vertically.** \- The selected Pattern will be flipped vertically.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to vertically flip a pattern in the 2D window using the Transform Pattern tool.

title: Flip Horizontally (2D)
content: **Flip Horizontally (2D)** \- Flip a Pattern horizontally in the 2D window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window and right click on the Pattern to be flipped and select **Flip Horizontally.** \- The selected Pattern will be flipped horizontally.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to flip a pattern horizontally in the 2D window using the Transform Pattern tool.

title: Delete Reference Line
content: **Delete Reference Line**** ** \- Delete the Reference Line originally created to use as a guide when editing a Pattern. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447968/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Right-click on the Pattern and select **Delete Reference Line** from the pop-up menu. \- The selected Pattern’s Reference Line will be deleted. \- Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021447988/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. Then, click and drag to move the desired point or line on the Pattern to confirm.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to delete a Reference Line in the Pattern editing process.

title: Cut
content: **List of Contents** Cut Use Cut **Cut** \- Cut Patterns based on the Internal Line. \- The CUT can be operated with following tools: * Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern** tool * Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Trace** tool ** Use Cut** \- Navigate to and select following tools: * Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern** tool * Trace tool \- Right-click on the Internal Line and select **Cut** from the pop-up menu. \- The Pattern will cut based on the Internal Line. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to use the Cut and Use Cut functions to edit patterns based on the Internal Line in a 2D design tool.

title: Convert to Curve Point
content: **Convert to Curve Point** \- Convert a segment point to a curve point. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021911008/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Navigate to the 2D window, right click on a segment point to be converted and select **Convert to Curve Point.** ** **\- The selected segment point will be converted to a curve point.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for converting a segment point to a curve point using the Edit Pattern tool in the 2D window.

title: Video Capture - Turn Table
content: **List of Contents** Turn Table Video Capture Record Turn Table Video Edit Turn Table Video Save Turn Table Video **Turn Table Video Capture** \- Record the 3D Garment in CLO to share with others for efficient communication. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Video Capture ▶ **Turn Table.** ** Record Turn Table Video** \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Video Capture ▶ **Turn Table.** \- The Turn Table Video Capture window will appear on the bottom of the window. \- Modify the options under the Video Size, Options, and the Video Codec sections. \- After adjusting the options as needed, select the **Record button.** \- When the recording is done, the preview window will appear. **Edit Turn Table Video** \- Edit the recording in the preview window. \- Split the video by right-clicking and selecting the **Split** option on the timeline bar. \- Then, select the timeline to be deleted and right click and select the **Delete** option. **Save Turn Table Video** \- Select the **Save** button to save the edited recording. \- Assign the saving path and the file name and click **Save.** \- The recording will be saved. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for capturing, editing, and saving 3D garment videos using the Turn Table feature in CLO software.

title: Project File Open/Save
content: **List of Contents** Project File Open Project File Overwrite Project File Save Project File **Project File** \- Save or open a file with 3D Garment, 3D Environment Settings (background, lighting, wind, camera, Simulation) animation information and more. ** Open Project File** \- Navigate to and select File ▶ Open ▶ **Project** \- The Open File Window will appear. \- Locate the file and select **Open.** **Overwrite Project File** \- A project file can be overwritten when a project file is already open. \- Navigate to and select File ▶ **Save Project.** \- The opened project file will be overwritten. **Save Project File** \- Navigate to and select File ▶ Save As ▶ **Project.** \- Designate the saving path and select **Save.** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides essential instructions for managing project files in a 3D design application, including how to open, save, and overwrite files.

title: 3D File (LXO) Export
content: **Objective** Export garments and avatars as LXO file format which is compatible with Modo. The LXO file format includes Geometry and Material information. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ **LXO** ** Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶**LXO** → The Save File window appears. 2. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, select **Save**. → The file is exported as a LXO file format.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for exporting garments and avatars as LXO files compatible with Modo, detailing the steps to save the necessary geometry and material information.
